thread: Follow the swarm underground, from fossil-bearing layers and sinking streams into sculpted caverns, then back out among crystals and mineral collections. Along the way, stone becomes a maze, a habitat, and a cabinet of strange shapes.

candidates.name: Kentucky Geological Survey
candidates.why: Fossil-bearing limestone, sinkholes, springs, mineral deposits, and geologic maps give the swarm a layered landscape to enter.

candidates.name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
candidates.why: Sulfuric-acid caves, immense chambers, cave formations, bats, and desert life offer a populated underground maze.

candidates.name: Mineralogy Museum of the Paris School of Mines
candidates.why: Minerals, gems, rocks, synthetic crystals, and unusual specimens furnish a cabinet of crystalline shapes for the swarm to inhabit.

candidates.name: National Cave and Karst Research Institute
candidates.why: Scalloped cave walls, stone fins, dripstone, springs, sinkholes, and cave environments make an alternate subterranean act.

candidates.name: GeoKansas
candidates.why: Kansas rocks, fossils, chalk formations, sinkholes, and geologic places offer another entrance into deep time.

candidates.name: Camborne School of Mines Virtual Museum
candidates.why: Mineral specimens, rock microscopy, mining heritage, and virtual field trips turn underground materials into a field laboratory.

candidates.name: Geevor Tin Mine
candidates.why: Underground workings, shafts, mining machinery, and the Hard Rock Museum introduce a human-made network through the stone.

candidates.name: British Geological Survey
candidates.why: Geological maps, rock and mineral resources, boreholes, and collections give the swarm many routes through the ground beneath Britain.
